testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: rebase-check job (pull_request-only branch-currency assertion, not meaningful in a worktree of origin/main); proc-macos job (node --test tests/proc.test.mjs on macOS) (subsumed by the full suite on this macOS host); smoke-omp job (needs pinned omp installed via bun, absent here); install-and-smoke job (needs pinned omp installed via bun and network, absent here).

unverified.claim: fleetIdentity uses the JS realpathSync, which keeps the case of the path as given, so on case-insensitive APFS an alarm file naming the same checkout spelled with different letter case is still refused with 'names fleet … restart omp'. realpathSync.native would match it.
unverified.evidence: `node probe.mjs copy/plugin/scripts/phase0.mjs` printed `REFUSE different case of checkout dir (case-insensitive APFS) ".../probe-yaTs80/REPO/.fleet" -> /private/var/.../REPO/.fleet` while fleetDir is `.../Repo/.fleet`. `node -e 'fs.realpathSync("/USERS/chris/.fleet/scratch")'` printed `/USERS/chris/.fleet/scratch`, and `fs.realpathSync.native(...)` printed `/Users/chris/.fleet/scratch`. [INFERENCE] Whether omp ever records a differently-cased cwd was not observed. The ticket's own measured failure, /var vs /private/var, MATCHes. The git top-level check that the ticket says to reuse has the same behaviour, so this is consistent with the existing code, not a regression.
unverified.suggested_fix: If 'whatever the spelling' should cover case on macOS, use realpathSync.native(dirname(path)) in fleetIdentity. Otherwise leave it as is, consistent with the git top-level check.

unverified.claim: The bare `catch {}` in fleetIdentity swallows every realpathSync error (ENOENT, EACCES, ELOOP, EMFILE, a NUL byte) and returns the raw path. It fails closed: an unresolvable path is compared as spelled, so it can only turn a would-be pass into a refusal. The refusal then reads `names fleet "X", not Y`, with no hint that resolution failed.
unverified.evidence: In a standalone probe, an unresolvable path came back unchanged and a resolvable one was canonicalised: `loop/.fleet`, `dangling/.fleet` and `link/sub/x/.fleet` (through a mode-000 dir) returned as given, and `link/.fleet` and `link/sub/../.fleet` became `real/.fleet`. Non-string, relative and empty inputs were returned as given. A transient EACCES/EMFILE on one side alone would give a refusal that looks like a different-fleet mismatch. This was not run end-to-end.
unverified.suggested_fix: Optional: narrow the catch to `e.code === "ENOENT"`, `ENOTDIR` or `ELOOP` and rethrow the rest. Or add `(path could not be resolved: <code>)` to the refusal text when either side fell back to the raw path.

unverified.claim: The catch-fallback branch is not pinned against a constant return. If the catch returns a fixed value instead of the raw path, all 112 phase0 tests still pass.
unverified.evidence: In my copy I changed the catch to `return "X";` and ran `node --test tests/phase0.test.mjs`: 112 tests, 112 pass, 0 fail. The refusal test's `no-such` case only exercises one unresolvable side, because the fixture's own `.fleet` dir always resolves. With two different unresolvable spellings, such a mutant would compare them equal and let a false alarm pass.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add a case where both rec.fleet and fleetDir are unresolvable and differ, expecting a refusal. Or unit-test fleetIdentity directly.

unverified.claim: Both new alarm tests discriminate: every mutant of fleetIdentity/the compare that I applied was killed by the named test, and the unmutated tree is green on the same narrowed run.
unverified.evidence: red: ./agent-test tests/phase0.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='alarm: a file naming' → exit 1, fail 1 incl 'alarm: a file naming this .fleet/ through a symlinked spelling passes…' (mutant A identity; mutant E realpath(whole path) gave the same); baseline: same cmd → exit 0, tests 112 pass 112, that test ✔. red: same cmd → exit 1, fail 1 incl 'alarm: a file naming another checkout's .fleet/ is refused, through a symlink or not, and so is a relative one' (mutant D, isAbsolute dropped); baseline: same cmd → exit 0, that test ✔. red: same cmd → exit 1, fail 2 incl the same 'refused' test (mutant C, check removed); baseline: same cmd → exit 0, that test ✔. No surviving mutant, so no coverage gap to report.

unverified.claim: The diff introduces no new types or casts, since it is plain .mjs. The invariant 'path is an absolute string' is enforced at runtime by fleetIdentity's typeof/isAbsolute guard, which falls back to the raw input, so it is a runtime check and not a type guarantee.
unverified.evidence: Read the diff; the only changed logic is `fleetIdentity(rec.fleet) !== fleetIdentity(fleetDir)`. A non-string or relative value is returned unchanged, so two equal relative spellings still compare equal, exactly as before the change. The new test covers a relative `.fleet` against an absolute fleetDir and expects it to be refused. I found no illegal state this change makes reachable.

unverified.claim: In the new symlink test, `assert.equal(r.stdout.includes("alarm threw"), false)` can never be the assertion that fails: the only source of that text is phase0.mjs:834, which turns a throw into a `failed` result, and that always exits 3 (phase0.mjs:848-857). So the `r.status === 0` check on the line before it, and the later `steps.alarm.status === "ok"` check, already catch every case it could catch.
unverified.evidence: grep `threw` phase0.mjs → only :834 `result = failed(`${name} threw: ${e.message}`)`; sed -n 826,860p shows failed → `stop = "failed"` → `process.exitCode = 3`. Mutant in the measuring copy: added `if (path.includes("/link/")) throw new Error("mutant");` to fleetIdentity, then ran `node --test --test-name-pattern="symlinked spelling" tests/phase0.test.mjs`. Output: `phase0: alarm: failed — alarm threw: mutant`, AssertionError `actual: 3, expected: 0` at tests/phase0.test.mjs:558:10. The status assertion stops the test first, so line 559 is never reached.
unverified.suggested_fix: Delete line 559 (`assert.equal(r.stdout.includes("alarm threw"), false);`). Optionally use `assert.match(r.stdout, /^phase0: alarm: ok/m)` instead, as the neighbouring 'a matching file passes' test does, if the printed status line should be checked.
